title: 생존을 위한 나만의 디자인 언어 만들기

content: 디자인은 기능적인 문제를 해결하는 것에서 한 걸음 더 나아가 사용 과정에 좋은 감각을 더할 수 있어야 한다고 생각합니다. 그렇다고 보여주기 위한 화려함을 뜻하는 것은 아닙니다. 작은 터치로 사용하는 즐거움을 더하되 기능의 흐름을 방해하거나 인터페이스 자체가 주인공이 되지 않아야 합니다. 서비스가 가진 가치를 더 잘 느끼게 만드는 것이 중요합니다.

title: VPC
content: 들어가며 최근 웹 서비스, 클라우드, 그리고 AI 애플리케이션 개발에서 인프라 구조를 이해하는 일은 점점 더 중요해지고 있습니다. 예전에는 서버 한 대에 웹 서버와 데이터베이스를 함께 올려 운영하는 경우도 많았지만, 요즘은 서비스 규모가 커지고 구조가 복잡해지면서 네트워크 설계 역시 중요한 요소가 되었습니다. AWS를 사용하다 보면 EC2, RDS, Load Balancer, NAT Gateway 같은 여러 서비스를 만나게 됩니다. 그리고 이 서비스들을 구성할 때 거의 항상 함께 등장하는 개념이 있습니다. 바로 VPC입니다. 처음에는 VPC라는 용어가 낯설 수 있습니다. Virtual Private Cloud라는 이름도 어렵게 느껴지고, Subnet, CIDR, Route Table, Internet Gateway, Security Group 같은 용어들이 한꺼번에 나오기 때문에 더 헷갈릴 수 있습니다. 하지만 VPC는 어렵게만 볼 개념은 아닙니다. 조금 쉽게 말하면, VPC는 클라우드 안에 만드는 우리 서비스만의…

title: Source Type’s Dictionary of the Illegible explores what happens when typography stops making sense
content: From metal band logos, watermelon emojis and comic book grawlixes to coded messages designed to evade online censorship, SourceType’s new book examines how illegible text can communicate and connect us.

title: The brand for Lance Oppenheim’s production company has chaos built in
content: Far from being one singular idea, Day Job’s brand for To Be Formed is the culmination of experimentation and playing with Oppenheim’s irreverent cinematic world.

title: Affinity and Cavalry give creatives somewhere to create freely… and for free
content: To explore the creative freedom of Affinity and Cavalry’s software, Melina K and Rob Farmer were tasked with using the free-to-use tools to depict somewhere they felt most unrestricted. The pair created a poster each, alongside a bespoke design kit that you can download and deploy in your own designs.

title: Carolina Incerti’s A Book for Making Books is designed to be torn apart and remade
content: The graphic designer’s hands-on guide transforms into eight different book and zine templates, inviting readers to explore self-publishing through experimentation and play.

title: See the process behind Laika’s stop-motion fantasy fable, Wildwood, in London exhibition
content: To coincide with the stop-motion studio’s upcoming release, London’s Design Museum welcomes Wildwood, exhibiting the inner workings and design of Laika’s nature-inspired epic.

title: Design disasters or creative solutions? The self-made paper signs replacing wayfinding in Singapore’s railway stations
content: As the Southeast Asian nation plans to expand its rail network to about 360 km by the early 2030s – matching cities such as Hong Kong, London, Tokyo and New York – station managers have designed their own signs to help passengers navigate the growing maze.

title: Fulham F.C gets a brand refresh built on hand-rendered lettering found on the walls of its stadium
content: Creative agency Music, in collaboration with F37 Foundry, translate the architectural references to Fulham as an area and the heritage of Fulham as a football team into a functioning type system.

title: Nik Arthur’s ultimate creative partner is the natural world in his organic animations for A24 and J. Cole
content: This experimental animator moulds natural elements around client briefs, utilising swamp waters and decaying plants in inventive stop motion capture.

title: Sex not Seggs – in a censored digital landscape, erotic commentary is freer on the printed page
content: Erotic Review director Lucy Roeber describes the brick walls the publication has faced in building an online presence as a result of landing in the ‘erotic dustbin’ of the internet – with limited room for expression and discussion.

title: Ancient wisdom, modern mark: the identity for SŌM’s daily elixir shots — The Brand Identity – Home of the Greatest in Graphic & Brand Design
content: SŌM is a Belgian brand of functional elixirs, and its flagship – the SŌM Power Elixir – is a daily shot for steady energy and mental clarity. It blends traditional ingredients from Colombia, including chontaduro and pitaya, with modern formulation. “The Colombian origin isn’t something we layered on at the end; it’s why the product exists,” explains Founder Laurenzo Van Mello.

title: Professional overthinking: how Thomas Pokorn designs brands with words — The Brand Identity – Home of the Greatest in Graphic & Brand Design
content: Strategist and copywriter Thomas Pokorn calls what he does “professional overthinking” – taking a client’s subject apart and putting it back together so that anyone can understand it. Freelance for more than a decade and based in New York since 2023, Pokorn usually works on a project from start to finish and stays for the design reviews, where the words and the design sharpen each other. In this conversation, we speak about why copywriting receives less attention than design, what separates a strategy that gets us…

title: Grafik’s Nick de Jardine on why websites “matter more than ever” — The Brand Identity – Home of the Greatest in Graphic & Brand Design
content: Since we last caught up in 2021, Nick de Jardine, the New Zealand-based designer and developer behind Grafik, has come to realise that, for a lot of businesses, a website is “the first place people actually experience the brand.” He has relaunched Grafik with a site built around that idea. Visitors can draw over it with 10 tools, including a piece of bread, and can submit their drawings to a public gallery where others can remix them. An experimental layer on the site lets AI agents find and use the same drawing t…

title: Studio Hi Ho pairs kraft and butter yellow in Madeleine’s packaging — The Brand Identity – Home of the Greatest in Graphic & Brand Design
content: Madeleine is a Melbourne-based cultured butter maker founded by Jack Gaffney, who returned to Australia after many years living in France with a dream to make butter using traditional methods. The malaxer, a historic butter-making machine that slowly kneads, folds and works the butter, is at the centre of its process. Malaxers were once commonplace in dairies, but they largely disappeared as butter production industrialised. Madeleine’s process is deliberately slower – grass-fed Jersey cow cream from West Gippslan…

title: How Red Antler’s brand helps Rovex’s robot feel familiar in hospitals — The Brand Identity – Home of the Greatest in Graphic & Brand Design
content: Rovi, the first product from Rovex, is what the hospital logistics platform describes as the first robot built to move patients. Rovi attaches to any stretcher and moves stable patients through the hospital on its own without major changes to the building’s infrastructure. New York-based Red Antler was commissioned to create the brand strategy, identity, messaging, digital and visual design, and art direction for the company.

title: Balense’s identity, by Willow & Blake, turns balance into a system — The Brand Identity – Home of the Greatest in Graphic & Brand Design
content: Balense® is a clinical skincare range that was born at Australian Skin Clinics. It had lived only as a product inside that clinic group, but GM & Brand Director Nicola Kropach had bigger ambitions to reformulate it for Gen Z. “I knew there was genuine brand equity in the Balense® name that we had never had the right partner to articulate properly,” she tells us. title: Hochburg’s identity for grill brand Flamid draws on maker’s marks — The Brand Identity – Home of the Greatest in Graphic & Brand Design
content: Flamid is a brand of insulated, modular grill barrels, made by hand in a metal workshop on the Swabian Alb in Germany. Every barrel shares the same core, built around fire, and takes on a different character through its outer shell – black steel, Corten steel that changes with weather and time, or a steel gabion cage that can be filled with stone. title: A founder with a tool is not a founder with a clue
content: Somewhere in this room is the one person who can tell if any of it is actually good. AI made everyone else look exactly like them. AI lets a solo founder produce a product, but it can’t help them understand whether that product is actually good…yet. That expertise, the hard-won judgment underneath it, has always been what decides who wins and who quietly (or epically) fails.
